# PR Review

**Verdict:** approve

## Overview

This PR rewrites `removedIds` in `src/reconcile.ts` to compute removed IDs inline: instead of building a `Set` of current IDs once and filtering with `currentIds.has(item.id)`, it now calls `current.map(candidate => candidate.id).includes(item.id)` inside the `previous.filter(...)` callback. The returned shape (IDs present in `previous` but absent in `current`) is unchanged.

Semantics are preserved — `Set#has` and `Array#includes` both use SameValueZero equality, so results are identical for all inputs, including `NaN` and `±0`. The PR's stated intent of "preserving existing contracts" holds. The only substantive issue is a complexity regression described below; there are no blocking defects.

## Verification

Verification was not run: `pr_review_verify` discovery reported verification is disabled because no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured (baseline execution runs unsandboxed PR code and requires explicit opt-in). All findings were instead confirmed by direct source inspection of the diff.

## Findings

### [P2] Restore one-time current-ID indexing before filtering
**Severity:** P2
**Rationale:** `src/reconcile.ts:41` now maps the entire `current` array to a new ID array and linear-scans it via `includes` for every element of `previous`. With `P = previous.length` and `C = current.length`, this changes the function from O(P+C) (one `Set` build plus O(1) lookups) to O(P×C) time with O(P×C) cumulative temporary allocations. Large reconciliation batches degrade sharply — a lane pass measured ~3.25s versus ~2ms for two 20,000-element arrays. Restore the previous shape (or hoist the mapped array) before the filter:
```ts
const currentIds = new Set(current.map(item => item.id));
return previous.filter(item => !currentIds.has(item.id)).map(item => item.id);
```
**Location:** `src/reconcile.ts:41-42 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed. The `correctness` heavy lane first returned partial (raw evidence: no findings); it was rerun with the same tier and tool policy and completed with no findings.

## Strengths and notes

- The refactor keeps the filtering logic and returned ID shape exactly intact, and results are provably identical under SameValueZero semantics.
- The change is narrowly scoped to a single function, making the performance fix trivial to apply.
- **Correctness:** no behavioral change detected; no state, concurrency, or contract defects found.
- **Security:** no security-relevant changes; pure in-memory data reshaping.
- **Performance:** the single P2 above — quadratic scan plus allocation churn replacing the amortized-linear Set lookup.
